_comment: Predictive Risk Agent (Phase 5) config. Tunable without code changes — edit and restart. RUL day-counts themselves live in data/fault_taxonomy.json (rul_days_stage_N); this file holds agent-level policy: failure-probability blend, risk-level source, business-impact flagging, the monitor band for undetermined faults, and logging.

failure_probability._comment: failure_probability = stage_base[iso_stage] blended with the anomaly_score. Weights must sum to 1.0. stage_base['0'] covers the undetermined/no-fault case (anomaly fired but no signature matched).

risk_level._comment: Reuse the Failure Intelligence severity (already escalated one level for high-criticality and/or bottleneck assets) as risk_level. This keeps risk_level and diagnosis.severity from diverging. fallback is used only when the diagnosis carries no severity.

business_impact._comment: business_impact_flag is raised for production bottlenecks and/or high-criticality assets.

monitor_band._comment: RUL band returned when iso_stage == 0 (undetermined fault — an anomaly fired but no taxonomy signature matched). No imminent timeline is quantified, so financial_exposure is forced to 0.
monitor_band.label: monitor

llm_fallback._comment: Optional LLM advisory layer for cases the rule engine cannot assess confidently. Set enabled=true and provide Azure AI Foundry credentials (AZURE_AI_ENDPOINT/KEY/DEPLOYMENT) or Azure OpenAI credentials (AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT/KEY/DEPLOYMENT) in .env. When unavailable, the deterministic assessment is always kept. The LLM augments the assessment with a recommended_action + rationale (advisory_note); the rule-based RUL/exposure numbers remain the auditable source of truth. For the undetermined/monitor case it may also set risk_level.
llm_fallback._trigger_undetermined_comment: Fire when iso_stage == 0 / no fault_code matched (rules give only a monitor band).
llm_fallback._trigger_conf_comment: Fire when diagnosis.confidence is below this threshold even if a fault matched. Set to 0 (default) to keep this trigger disabled — a matched fault means the rules DO have coverage and the LLM should not second-guess them.
llm_fallback._hitl_comment: When true, interactive runners (run_risk_demo.py, test_llm_fallback.py) pause after the LLM returns an advisory and ask the operator to Accept / Modify / Reject before the note is applied to the assessment. Programmatic callers (tests) leave hitl_handler=None so this flag has no effect.
